marks.gloss_en: Rav Sheshet, when he bowed, bowed like a cane
שנאמר גם אנכי חלילה לי מחטא לה' מחדל להתפלל בעדכם -- Samuel calls ceasing to pray for others a sin
whoever can ask mercy for his fellow and does not ask is called a sinner
אילימא משום דכתיב ואין חלה מכם עלי -- Saul expected his men to be ill over him
דילמא מלך שאני -- perhaps a king is different; Saul's verse does not reach a Torah scholar as such
אלא מהכא: ואני בחלותם לבושי שק -- David afflicted himself when they were ill
'and there is none of you that is ill over me or reveals to my ear' (I Sam 22:8, Saul)
if he [the one in need] is a Torah scholar, one must make himself ill over him
שנאמר ויגבה ה' צבאות במשפט והאל הקדוש נקדש בצדקה -- the verse speaks of the ten days (ויגבה... במשפט) and still says האל הקדוש
even if he said 'the holy God' [in the ten days], he has discharged his obligation
והלכתא כרבה -- in the ten days: המלך הקדוש
והלכתא כרבה -- in the ten days: המלך המשפט
Rav Yosef: [in the ten days one prays] 'the holy God'
throughout the year one prays 'the holy God'
דילמא צבור שאני -- perhaps a community is different [and Ezekiel's forgiveness of the community shows nothing about an individual]
the stam's replacement source: Saul told Samuel that God no longer answered him 'by prophets or by dreams' (1 Sam 28:15) -- and did not say 'by the Urim veTumim'
לימא פרשת רבית ופרשת משקלות דכתיב בהן יציאת מצרים -- then let them say the parasha of usury or of weights, in which the Exodus is written
(entertained) they sought to fix Balak because the Exodus is written in it -- 'God who brought them out of Egypt' (Num 23:22)
ולימא האי פסוקא ותו לא -- then let them say this verse and no more
גמירי: כל פרשה דפסקה משה רבינו פסקינן, דלא פסקה משה רבינו לא פסקינן -- the verse cannot be recited apart from its parasha (= p_gemiri_parasha_moshe)
a received tradition: any parasha that Moshe Rabbeinu divided we divide; one that Moshe Rabbeinu did not divide we do not divide
whoever commits a transgression and is ashamed of it -- all his sins are forgiven him
[he omitted the Urim veTumim] because he had killed Nov, the city of priests
Saul was pardoned from heaven
the Rabbis' source for the pardon: 'we will hang them up unto the Lord in the Giva of Saul, the chosen of the Lord' (2 Sam 21:6) -- a bat kol went out and said 'the chosen of the Lord'
they sought to fix parashat Balak in the recitation of the Shema
R' Yosei bar Avin: they sought to fix Balak because this verse is written in it -- 'he couched, he lay down like a lion and a lioness; who shall rouse him?' (Num 24:9)
R' Yehuda bar Chaviva: parashat tzitzit was fixed because there are five things in it
the yoke of mitzvot is explicit: 'and you shall see it and remember all the mitzvot of the Lord' (Num 15:39)
the baraita: 'after your hearts' -- this is heresy; and so it says, 'the fool said in his heart, there is no God' (Ps 14:1)
'kol yemei chayecha' -- the amplifying 'kol' adds the nights: the Exodus is mentioned in the evening Shema
Ben Zoma's allocation: 'the days of your life' -- the days; 'ALL' adds the nights
'kol' includes the days of the Messiah: the Exodus will still be mentioned then
the Sages' allocation: 'the days of your life' -- this world; 'ALL' includes the days of the Messiah
Ben Zoma: is the Exodus mentioned in the Messiah's days? Jeremiah says 'they shall NO LONGER say, As the Lord lives who brought up Israel out of Egypt'
not that the Exodus be uprooted from its place -- the subjugation of the kingdoms becomes principal and the Exodus subordinate to it
the Sages' answer: in the Messiah's days the Exodus is not uprooted; the subjugation of the kingdoms becomes principal and the Exodus subordinate
כיוצא בו אתה אומר: לא יקרא שמך עוד יעקב -- and Yaakov is not thereby uprooted; so too the Exodus under the future redemption
the Exodus is mentioned at night (in the evening Shema's third paragraph)
